question.text: Empiric treatment of uncomplicated urinary tract infection with fluoroquinolones in older women in Israel: another lost treatment option?
question.context: Current guidelines for the treatment of uncomplicated urinary tract infection (UTI) in women recommend empiric therapy with antibiotics for which local resistance rates do not exceed 10-20%. We hypothesized that resistance rates of Escherichia coli to fluoroquinolones may have surpassed this level in older women in the Israeli community setting. To identify age groups of women in which fluoroquinolones may no longer be appropriate for empiric treatment of UTI. Resistance rates for ofloxacin were calculated for all cases of uncomplicated UTI diagnosed during the first 5 months of 2005 in a managed care organization (MCO) in Israel, in community-dwelling women aged 41-75 years. The women were without risk factors for fluoroquinolone resistance. Uncomplicated UTI was diagnosed with a urine culture positive for E. coli. The data set was stratified for age, using 5 year intervals, and stratum-specific resistance rates (% and 95% CI) were calculated. These data were analyzed to identify age groups in which resistance rates have surpassed 10%. The data from 1291 urine cultures were included. The crude resistance rate to ofloxacin was 8.7% (95% CI 7.4 to 10.2). Resistance was lowest among the youngest (aged 41-50 y) women (3.2%; 95% CI 1.11 to 5.18), approached 10% in women aged 51-55 years (7.1%; 95% CI 3.4 to 10.9), and reached 19.86% (95% CI 13.2 to 26.5) among the oldest women (aged 56-75 y).

medgemma_4b.clinical_reasoning: The study found that fluoroquinolone resistance rates increased significantly with age in Israeli women with uncomplicated UTIs. The resistance rate was lowest in the 41-50 age group and increased to 19.86% in the 56-75 age group. This indicates that fluoroquinolones are no longer appropriate for empiric treatment in older women in this population.
medgemma_4b.critical_evidence: The resistance rate to ofloxacin reached 19.86% among women aged 56-75 years, exceeding the 10% threshold.
medgemma_4b.differential_considered: While other antibiotics might be considered, the study specifically focuses on fluoroquinolones. Other potential causes of UTI were not investigated in this study.

rnj1_8b.clinical_reasoning: The study found that resistance rates to ofloxacin were below the 10% threshold in all age groups except the oldest (56-75 years) at 19.86%. Since the question asks if fluoroquinolones are a 'lost treatment option' for older women, and only the oldest group exceeded 10%, the answer is no, as fluoroquinolones remain appropriate for most older women in this population.
rnj1_8b.critical_evidence: Resistance rate of 19.86% in the oldest group (56-75 years) was the highest, but still below the 20% threshold where guidelines recommend alternative therapy.
rnj1_8b.differential_considered: No other age groups exceeded the 10% resistance threshold, so no alternative treatment options were indicated based on this data.

qwen3_vl_8b.clinical_reasoning: The study shows that fluoroquinolone resistance in E. coli among older Israeli women (aged 56-75) reached 19.86%, far exceeding the 10-20% threshold considered acceptable for empiric therapy. This indicates fluoroquinolones are no longer appropriate for empiric treatment in this age group. The resistance rate is statistically significant and clinically relevant, supporting the conclusion that this treatment option is lost for this population.
qwen3_vl_8b.critical_evidence: Resistance rate of 19.86% (95% CI 13.2 to 26.5) in women aged 56-75 years exceeds the 10% threshold for acceptable empiric fluoroquinolone use.
qwen3_vl_8b.differential_considered: Other age groups (41-50, 51-55) had lower resistance rates (<10%), so the issue is age-specific. No other pathogens or confounders were mentioned, and the study focused solely on E. coli in uncomplicated UTI, ruling out alternative etiologies or risk factors.

olmo3_7b.critical_evidence: Resistance rates in women aged 56-75 years reached 19.86%, surpassing the recommended threshold for empirical use of fluoroquinolones.
olmo3_7b.differential_considered: I considered other antibiotics (like nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole) that may have lower resistance in older women, but the key issue is the specific exceedance of the fluoroquinolone resistance limit in the oldest subgroup, making them inappropriate for empirical treatment in that age range.
